idiom_name: memberwise initializer with default values (SE-0242) and trailing-closure configuration; @resultBuilder for hierarchies
implementation_notes: Swift synthesizes a memberwise initializer that carries a default for every property that has one (SE-0242, Swift 5.1), so Server(host: "db", maxConns: 10) already is the named, order-free, partially defaulted constructor a builder would provide, and producing a variant is var b = a; b.port = 9000 or a small with-style helper. For hierarchical products Swift uses @resultBuilder (SE-0289) instead - SwiftUI's ViewBuilder turns a sequence of statements into a value, which is the declarative analogue of a Director-driven builder. Keep a hand-written builder when construction is staged, performs effects, or must validate cross-field rules before an instance exists.
code_sketch:
struct Server {
    var host: String
    var port: Int = 8080
    var maxConns: Int = 100
}

let a = Server(host: "db")          // memberwise init applies the defaults
var b = a
b.maxConns = 10                     // variant without a builder type
pitfalls: The memberwise initializer is only synthesized when the type declares no initializer of its own; adding one init outside an extension removes the named/default constructor for every caller.
Classes get no memberwise initializer at all, so a class with many optional settings still needs a hand-written init or a builder.
@resultBuilder closures only produce a value through the builder's buildBlock methods: they cannot enforce cross-field validation or hand out a partially configured product.
